reason: Both conversations ruled out blockages and only reached the safety stop after the homeowner volunteered the burning smell; neither proactively asked about smells or sparking, though Conversation 2's 'stop if it smells hot' nudge is what surfaced the smell. Conversation 1 then asked the homeowner to inspect the motor bearings themselves (beyond their skill and tools) and closed by declaring the machine 'not worth attempting a repair' and recommending disposal, which is wrong for a Henry whose brushes or motor are routinely replaceable and contradicts the expected repairer escalation. Conversation 2 wasted a turn on an irrelevant floorhead/brush-bar check and its final message was thin, but it was honest about uncertainty, correctly pointed to a repairer, declined to name a part, and gave an appropriate stop-and-unplug instruction.
